questions.accessible_text:
1. [Maximum mark: 6]

Seven men have waist x:58,63,75,82,93,98,105 and BMI y:19,20,22,23,25,24,26. Model y=ax+b. (a)(i) Write a,b; (ii) find correlation coefficient. [4] (b) Estimate BMI for waist 95 cm. [2]
questions.summary: Seven men have waist x:58,63,75,82,93,98,105 and BMI y:19,20,22,23,25,24,26. Model y=ax+b. (a)(i) Write a,b; (ii) find correlation coefficient. [4] (b) Estimate BMI for waist 95 cm
questions.solution: Regression gives a=0.1411205…, b=11.1424… and r=0.977564…. Thus a=0.141,b=11.1,r=0.978. At x=95, y=24.5489…, so BMI≈24.5. This agrees with the official markscheme.

questions.accessible_text:
2. [Maximum mark: 5]

Let f(x)=4−2e^x. [Diagram: decreasing exponential crossing the axes.] (a) Find x-intercept. [2] (b) The region enclosed by f, both axes is rotated 360° about x-axis. Find volume. [3]
questions.summary: Let f(x)=4−2e^x. [Diagram: decreasing exponential crossing the axes.] (a) Find x-intercept. [2] (b) The region enclosed by f, both axes is rotated 360° about x-axis. Find volume. [
questions.solution: (a) 4−2e^x=0 gives x=ln2. (b) V=π∫₀^ln2(4−2e^x)²dx=π[16x−16e^x+2e^(2x)]₀^ln2=π(16ln2−10)=3.43 cm³. This agrees with the official markscheme.

3. [Maximum mark: 7]

Quadrilateral ABCD has AB=6.73 cm, BC=4.83 cm, angle BCD=78.2°, CD=3.80 cm. [Diagram: diagonal BD, angle BAD=θ.] (a) Find BD. [3] (b) Area of triangle ABD is 18.5 cm²; find possible θ. [4]
questions.summary: Quadrilateral ABCD has AB=6.73 cm, BC=4.83 cm, angle BCD=78.2°, CD=3.80 cm. [Diagram: diagonal BD, angle BAD=θ.] (a) Find BD. [3] (b) Area of triangle ABD is 18.5 cm²; find possibl
questions.solution: (a) Cosine rule in BCD gives BD=√(4.83²+3.80²−2·4.83·3.80cos78.2°)=5.50 cm. (b) 18.5=(1/2)(6.73)(5.501)sinθ, so sinθ=0.99939…; θ=88.0° or 92.0°. This agrees with the official markscheme.

questions.accessible_text:
4. [Maximum mark: 7]

OAB is a sector radius r and angle θ, 0<θ<π/2. C lies on OA and BC⊥OA. [Diagram: right triangle OBC inside sector.] (a) Show OC=rcosθ. [1] (b) Find area OBC in r,θ. [2] (c) If triangle area is 3/5 sector area, find θ. [4]
questions.summary: OAB is a sector radius r and angle θ, 0<θ<π/2. C lies on OA and BC⊥OA. [Diagram: right triangle OBC inside sector.] (a) Show OC=rcosθ. [1] (b) Find area OBC in r,θ. [2] (c) If tria
questions.solution: (a) In right triangle OBC, cosθ=OC/OB=OC/r. (b) BC=rsinθ, so area=(1/2)r²sinθcosθ. (c) Equating this to (3/5)(1/2r²θ) gives sinθcosθ=3θ/5. Numerical solution is θ=0.830 rad. This agrees with the official markscheme.

questions.accessible_text:
5. [Maximum mark: 6]

Fish population f(t)=1000/(1+24e^(−0.2t)), 0≤t≤30 months. (a) Find population at t=10. [2] (b) Find rate of increase then. [2] (c) Find t when increasing most rapidly. [2]
questions.summary: Fish population f(t)=1000/(1+24e^(−0.2t)), 0≤t≤30 months. (a) Find population at t=10. [2] (b) Find rate of increase then. [2] (c) Find t when increasing most rapidly. [2]
questions.solution: (a) f(10)=235 fish. (b) f′(10)=36.0 fish/month. (c) Logistic growth is fastest at half carrying capacity: 24e^(−0.2t)=1, so t=ln24/0.2=15.9 months. This agrees with the official markscheme.

questions.accessible_text:
6. [Maximum mark: 7]

In x³(1/(2x)+x²)^15, find the exact constant term.
questions.summary: In x³(1/(2x)+x²)^15, find the exact constant term.
questions.solution: A general choice of four x² factors and eleven 1/(2x) factors has net exponent 3+8−11=0. Constant coefficient=C(15,4)/2^11=1365/2048. This agrees with the official markscheme.

questions.accessible_text:
7. [Maximum mark: 6]

The vector equation of line L is r=(−1,3,8)+t(4,5,−1). Point P is the point on L that is closest to the origin. Find the coordinates of P.
questions.summary: Find the point on r=(−1,3,8)+t(4,5,−1) that is closest to the origin.
questions.solution: At the closest point, OP is perpendicular to the direction vector (4,5,−1). A general point is P=(−1+4t,3+5t,8−t). Hence (−1+4t,3+5t,8−t)·(4,5,−1)=0, so −4+16t+15+25t−8+t=0, giving 42t+3=0 and t=−1/14. Therefore P=(−9/7,37/14,113/14), approximately (−1.29,2.64,8.07).

8. [Maximum mark: 16]

Particle A has s_A=15−t−6t³e^(−0.8t), 0≤t≤25. [Graph: oscillatory displacement crossing axis.] (a) Initial displacement. [2] (b) First reaches P. [2] (c) First changes direction. [2] (d) Total distance first 3 s. [3] Particle B has v_B=8−2t. (e)(i) Given same start, find s_B; (ii) other meeting time. [7]
questions.summary: Particle A has s_A=15−t−6t³e^(−0.8t), 0≤t≤25. [Graph: oscillatory displacement crossing axis.] (a) Initial displacement. [2] (b) First reaches P. [2] (c) First changes direction. [
questions.solution: (a) s_A(0)=15 cm. (b) First positive root s_A=0 is t=2.469… s. (c) Solving v_A=s_A′=0 gives t=4.077… s. (d) Before 3 s motion is one direction, so distance=|s_A(3)−15|=17.696…=17.7 cm. (e) Integrating gives s_B=8t−t²+C; C=15, so s_B=15+8t−t². Solving s_A=s_B gives the other meeting at t=9.304…=9.30 s. This agrees with the official markscheme.

9. [Maximum mark: 14]

At an airport P(A)=0.70, P(D)=0.85, P(A∩D)=0.65. (a) Show A,D not independent. [2] (b)(i) Find P(A∩D′); (ii) P(D′|A). [5] Pilot weekly hours ~N(25,σ²), with 90% below 28. (c) Find σ. [3] (d) Flights have two pilots; find percentage where both flew over 30 h. [4]
questions.summary: At an airport P(A)=0.70, P(D)=0.85, P(A∩D)=0.65. (a) Show A,D not independent. [2] (b)(i) Find P(A∩D′); (ii) P(D′|A). [5] Pilot weekly hours ~N(25,σ²), with 90% below 28. (c) Find
questions.solution: (a) P(A)P(D)=0.595≠0.65. (b) P(A∩D′)=0.70−0.65=0.05; conditional=0.05/0.70=1/14. (c) (28−25)/σ=1.28155, so σ=2.34. (d) P(X>30)=1−Φ(5/2.3409)=0.0164; squaring for independent pilots gives 0.000269, or 0.0269%. This agrees with the official markscheme.
